    1/8Overview

    Teaching evaluation to tell right from finished

    Agent evaluation could prove an agent finished its task, not that its answer was right. I designed how AI practitioners create ground truth, the answer key every score is checked against: an agent drafts it, a person verifies it, and only then does anything depend on it.

    Role
    Product designer, end to end
    Product
    Ground truth in Now Assist Skill Kit
    Timeline
    Q4 2025 to Q4 2026
    Status
    Live internally; customer flow in design

    What I owned

    • Framing. Turned "manual or automated?" into a decision about trust, and wrote the principles the flow follows.
    • Structure. Placed curation in the practitioner's journey and defined the IA and flow, including the one step nobody can skip.
    • Interaction and UI. The home, the entry point and the three-step curation flow: 13 states, end to end.
    • Failure cases. Records that never ran, bad runs, version drift, review that outlasts one sitting, values the machine guessed.
    • Alongside. Platform on the standalone data model; data science on the curation agent.

    01Understand

    Finished isn't the same as right

    Our metrics checked that a task completed, which tools ran and the path the agent took. None of that says whether the outcome was correct, because there was nothing to compare it against.

    Teams were already doing it by hand

    Checked by hand. Business units compared agent output against ground truth manually, for their top customers.

    Built one-off. Implementation teams had written ground truth generators for single enterprise customers.

    First customers named. Leadership review confirmed aviation and banking accounts would use it first.

    It worked internally. Customers couldn't touch it.

    Three ground truth metrics went live for internal users in Q4 2025. A script wrote the records; people edited them as raw JSON.

    To reach customers, three things had to change

    • AuthoringDesign led, meA flow to select, generate, review and edit. No list views, no raw JSON.
    • Data modelPlatformA standalone table: use case, source record, payload. Nothing that leans on internal tables.
    • CurationData scienceAn agent instead of a script, so new records aren't stranded and failed runs aren't copied in as answers.

    02Define

    A practitioner, not a labeller

    The person who needs ground truth builds agents for a living. If authoring feels like a second job, they'll skip it, so it had to fit work they were already doing.

    Sam

    AI practitioner

    Builds agents and skills, creates datasets, iterates. Ground truth is one task among many.

    Not a dedicated data labeller

    Needs to

    • Know the answer is right, not just finished
    • Check tools ran with the right inputs, in order
    • See where the agent diverges, without reading logs
    • Iterate without re-authoring ground truth

    Designing against

    • One reference spans tool calls, decisions and outputs
    • The work crosses AI Agent Studio, Skill Kit and Data Kit
    • Runs come from execution logs and AutoChat
    • Some records have never been run

    Curation has a right moment

    After the agent roughly works, before anyone trusts a number.

    1. 1Build and testSingle-record tests until there's a stable baseline.
    2. 2Create and review ground truthAutogenerate, review, save. Review can wait for later.This project
    3. 3Evaluate and iterateGround truth metrics beside reference-free ones, scored per record.

    A run looks right? Nudge to capture it as ground truth.

    Back here only if the use case changes

    Improve, re-run, reuse the same ground truth

    Authoring is paid once per use case. That's what makes a required review affordable.

    03Decide

    It looked like a cost question. It was a trust question.

    Manual curation is accurate but slow. Automated curation is fast but leans toward the model that wrote it. Picking one meant giving up either scale or trust.

    • ManualNuanced and accurate on edge cases. Slow, costly, open to human bias.
    • AutomatedFast and varied. Biased toward its own model, with no view of its quality.
    • HybridAn agent drafts at speed; a person verifies before anything depends on it.

    What settled it

    Low scores get blamed on the agent. Look closer and the ground truth is often what was wrong. If the reference is wrong, every score built on it is a confident lie.

    So: automate for speed, and make review a step nobody can skip.

    1. Agent
    2. Records
    3. Autogenerate
    4. Review and save

    Six rules the flow follows

    Each traces back to the problem analysis or the leadership review. The screens cite them by number.

    1. 1Autogenerate, never auto-trustGeneration assists. Verification is human and required.
    2. 2One destination, not threeNavigation and the primary action hold position across every step.
    3. 3Empty isn't brokenA state you haven't reached names the next action. Errors are for errors.
    4. 4Name things the way a person wouldPre-filled, editable names, because datasets get found again months later.
    5. 5Show the seam between machine and humanGenerated and verified are separate progress, so it's clear what still needs judgement.
    6. 6Make ground truth traceableEvery record carries where it came from, so a surprising score can be traced back.

    6Traceable

    Step 1, screen 1 of 4

    Configure once, then collapse

    Input type and a pre-filled, editable name, answering feedback that names were cryptic. A suggested set, a pattern borrowed from another team, pre-selects runs fit for ground truth.

    4Human names

    Step 1, screen 2 of 4

    Records left, detail right

    The selection count stays visible while the detail pane pages through records, showing the utterance each run was tested with.

    2One destination

    Step 1, screen 3 of 4

    Check a run before promoting it

    Execution plan, conversation log, related record and status, each linked, so a failed run doesn't quietly become the reference.

    6Traceable

    Step 1, screen 4 of 4

    No history? Start from records

    Pick table records instead of runs. Utterance and context can be autogenerated, then copied to every record, which the old script couldn't do at all.

    3Empty isn't broken

    Step 2, screen 1 of 3

    Aspects, not JSON

    Each aspect states what it is, how it's checked and what it looks like, so the toggle explains its own consequence: what you'll review next, and which metrics can use it.

    1Never auto-trust

    Step 2, screen 2 of 3

    Order becomes part of the answer

    Expected tool sequence joins the set instead of hiding behind a custom metric. Sequencing proved hard to engineer, so its metric comes later.

    Step 2, screen 3 of 3

    A named commitment point

    Starting curation locks the selections, and says so before the machine takes over. For now, curated sets are create-only.

    1Never auto-trust

    Step 3, screen 1 of 4

    Two progress bars, on purpose

    Generated and verified are tracked apart, so machine progress is never mistaken for sign-off. Each record keeps its status, and review can wait: exit and verify later.

    5Show the seam

    Step 3, screen 2 of 4

    Match per field, guesses flagged

    Each field picks exact, semantic or contains. Values the AI suggested carry a tag, so reviewers know which cells deserve a second look.

    5Show the seam

    Step 3, screen 3 of 4

    Tool expectations, no hand-edited JSON

    Agent, tool, order, match and expected output in one dialog, with the raw JSON a tab away for anyone who wants it.

    Step 3, screen 4 of 4

    Provenance on every record

    The execution plan, the conversation and related records travel with each reference, so a surprising score can be argued instead of just regretted.

    6Traceable

      A wrong reference fails quietly

      It doesn't throw an error. It just makes every score built on it wrong. These are the moments I designed for, shown where they're handled on the real screens.

      Build from table records instead. Utterance and context are autogenerated, then copied to every record, so new records aren't stranded.

      Check the run before it's promoted. Its plan, conversation and status are one click away, and suggested sets pre-select suitable runs.

      Version is required up front. A dataset stays tied to the agent version it was authored for.

      Progress is split, and nothing is lost. Generated and verified are tracked apart, every record keeps its status, and you can exit and verify later.

      Guesses are flagged. AI-suggested values carry a tag, and each field sets its own match: exact, semantic or contains.

      The reference can be traced. Every record keeps its execution plan, conversation and source, so the score can be checked and argued.

      05Validate

      Live internally, earning its way to customers

      Three ground truth metrics already run for internal users. Reaching customers takes a standalone data model, a curation agent, and testing this flow with the people it's for.

      Next:Heuristic evaluationInternal usability testsCustomer research

      Still open

      Questions the next round of testing and review has to answer.

      • Does ground truth need versions?Rollback and audit, against storage and interface weight.
      • Where should curation live?Data Kit centralises datasets; evaluation saves a trip. Leadership leaned toward one studio.
      • Should these scores feed optimisation?A comparison may be too thin to suggest a fix.
      • How do generated runs stay predictable?An AutoChat run can take a route a good reference never expected.
      • Does conversational ground truth fit?It has its own idea of an expected outcome.
      • Can production become the authoring surface?Admins already judge output while running agents.

      What I'd carry forward

      1. The hard part wasn't the payloadI expected the challenge to be a complex JSON structure. It was sequencing, naming and orientation; the structure got easy once people stopped getting lost.
      2. Trust is a UI problem tooA score is only as good as its reference, so where each reference came from has to be on screen. Here, provenance is the point, not a power-user extra.
      3. Test before addingNew features on an unvalidated flow inherit its problems. The order is fixed: a heuristic pass, then real users, then the next features.

      Evaluation is only as right as its answer key. This flow lets an agent draft the key, and makes sure a person signs it before anything is graded against it.
